turns.text: hi! can u make a clean one page graphic + label layout for lola's roll showing cost and nutrition per roll pls

Happy to! To make it accurate I need the numbers. Could you send the cost per roll and the nutrition facts (calories, fat, sodium, etc.), plus how many rolls go in a serving or tray? And is this for a printed label, a menu card, or both?

ok im pulling the numbers from jun's sheet, just finished them today

per roll: cost $0.84, 92 cal, 5g fat, 8g carbs, 4g protein, 210mg sodium

its for the saturday cafe counter trays jun sells. both a little tray label and a one page info graphic

Here's the plan, using only your numbers.

[Image: A clean one-page graphic on a warm off-white background. Title at top: "Lola's Roll" in bold rounded type with a small lumpia icon. Subtitle: "Per roll at a glance." Center: a row of five rounded tiles, each with a big number and a small label:
- Calories: 92
- Fat: 5g
- Carbs: 8g
- Protein: 4g
- Sodium: 210mg
Below, a wide banner tile: "Cost per roll: $0.84" with a thin bar showing the cost breakdown placeholder [ingredient split]. Footer: "Available Saturdays at the cafe counter." Palette: warm orange, deep green, cream.]

[Image: A tray label, 4 x 2.5 in landscape. Left: "Lola's Roll" logo and "Lumpia". Right: a mini nutrition box titled "Per roll" with Calories 92, Fat 5g, Carbs 8g, Protein 4g, Sodium 210mg. Bottom strip: [price per roll] and [allergen line].]

Two things to fill in: the selling price and an allergen line, since I don't have those. Want me to change the colors or font?
love it. can u make the numbers bigger and the colors match green/pink? i gotta finish before anatomy review and chem lecture later

Done, quick version:

[Image: The same one-page graphic, restyled. Background soft cream. Title in deep green. The five tiles now alternate green and pink, with the numbers roughly 40% larger in bold white or dark green for contrast. The cost banner is pink with "$0.84 cost per roll" in large type. Footer unchanged.]

[Image: The tray label in the same green and pink, with the nutrition numbers enlarged and the "Per roll" box outlined in green.]
